evidence: The verify step pipes the manifest through `jq` with no prior assertion, while every other builder capability is proved in `reachability` before the build; the agent agreed it was present today but unasserted and moved the check into `reachability`.
guidance_note: When a pipeline already has a preflight job for host capabilities, add every non-coreutils tool the later jobs invoke to that job in the original PR.

evidence: The doc recipe sent only the Docker manifest Accept header while the workflow sends both Docker and OCI headers, and the doc itself says the header is load-bearing; the agent added the OCI header and reasonably declined extracting a shared script for one curl call.
guidance_note: When a doc reproduces a command the code also runs, copy it from the code verbatim and diff the two before pushing.

evidence: 74bb522 added `echo "jq: $(jq --version)"` under `set -euo pipefail`; the agent's own repro shows `echo` returns 0 when the substitution fails, so the F1 fix asserted nothing.
guidance_note: When adding a fail-fast assertion, run it once with the dependency removed (e.g. PATH=/nonexistent) and confirm it exits non-zero before naming it the fix.

evidence: False-positive flag: 74bb522 only added the jq step and the CLAUDE.md Accept header, and the label-compose heredoc is original PR code. The premise is overstated because `set -u` already aborts on unset variables, but set-but-empty was a real hole; a check over the composed block for lines ending in `=` covers every label, including ones added later.
guidance_note: When validating one interpolated input into a composed artifact, validate the composed artifact so every field is covered, not just the one that motivated the check.

evidence: Same defect as F3, on the same line from 74bb522: `echo` masks the exit status of `jq --version` under errexit. The agent fixed both with one change in 4919f74.
guidance_note: When adding a fail-fast assertion, exercise its failure path before pushing; a check verified only green is unverified.

evidence: 74bb522 added a fourth proof to `reachability`, but CLAUDE.md line 21 still listed three. The agent: "the enumeration is stale and I made it stale."
guidance_note: When a fix adds a step to a job, grep the docs for any enumeration of what that job proves and update it in the same commit.

evidence: False-positive flag: the digest paragraph is original PR text that 74bb522 did not touch. The premise holds because `gdn.sanctuary.build.run` and `image.version` carry the run id and tag, so a re-dispatch of an unchanged commit also changes the digest.
guidance_note: When documenting a consequence of stamped metadata, derive it from every field being stamped, not from the headline field.

narrative: Round 0 raised a missing jq preflight and a doc header drift. The jq fix (74bb522) was a no-op under errexit and was flagged twice (F3, F5); it also left the CLAUDE.md enumeration stale (F6). Round 1 also raised two findings on original code (F4, F7), so round 2 would have happened anyway. All round-1 fixes landed in 4919f74 and round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent verified the jq step only on the green runner and never ran the failure path, which is the one path a preflight exists for.
Each fix added a fact to a job without sweeping the docs that enumerate that job.

evidence: README hardcodes the gitea remote URL, while CLAUDE.md says to read it from `git remote -v` and "not from this document". The thread is resolved with no reply and marked outdated, so the region changed in 2ae6227, but the packet has no diff showing what changed.
guidance_note: Before writing a fact into a second doc, check whether the first doc has a stated policy about that fact.

evidence: This duplicates F1: the hardcoded gitea URL contradicts CLAUDE.md's instruction not to trust a written-down remote. It was resolved without a reply, and the packet does not show the eventual change.

README does restate the tag format and the verify sequence that the workflow and CLAUDE.md own, but a README summary of the deploy path is a legitimate audience-specific doc, so 'three copies' overstates the harm. The thread was resolved without a reply and the packet shows no diff.
guidance_note: In a README, summarize the mechanism in one line and point at the owning file for tag formats and job conditions instead of restating them.

evidence: README repeats the trigger and job-condition wording that CLAUDE.md already has ("no mirror, no polling, no schedule"). The drift risk is real but minor for a README. The thread was resolved silently and the packet has no diff for 2ae6227.

narrative: This is a docs-only deletion PR. Round 0 raised two duplicate findings about the hardcoded gitea URL and two about README restating workflow facts. The agent resolved all four threads with no reply; the threads went outdated and round 1 approved, but the packet does not show what 2ae6227 changed.
guidance_observations: All four threads were resolved with no reply, so nothing records whether each finding was fixed, rejected, or narrowed.

evidence: The README block runs `uv run ... main.py` (a foreground server) followed by `cargo test` as if sequential. The agent admitted the server was actually backgrounded in another shell when they ran it.
guidance_note: Write a 'run it yourself' recipe as the literal sequence of shells and commands you executed, not a condensed block.

narrative: A rename and doc PR with a single finding: the README recipe would hang on the foreground server. It was fixed in ce971a3 with two terminals and a readiness check, and round 1 approved.

evidence: The error text listed "(macOS: metal, Linux: cuda)", restating the per-target list that Cargo.toml's own comment says must be the complete one. The agent replaced it with a pointer.
guidance_note: When writing an error message, do not enumerate a list another file declares authoritative; point at that file.

evidence: The agent confirmed that `whisper_print_system_info` reports compile-time flags only and narrowed the comment, which was one of the reviewer's offered options. But the new comment claimed "each way of losing the GPU lands somewhere loud", which F4 showed was false for a backend that fails to initialise.
guidance_note: When correcting an overclaiming comment, enumerate the failure modes explicitly and write only what each is verified to do, not a new completeness claim.

evidence: bef09c8 rewrote the NoAcceleration text to add "a container without the GPU fails ... at the dynamic loader, on libcuda.so.1". That claim is false on exactly the targets that reach this variant. The agent: "my previous fix relocated the defect instead of removing it."
guidance_note: When a fix removes a duplicated fact from a shared error message, check that every sentence added in its place holds on every path that reaches the message.

evidence: F2 had already pointed at residual silent CPU fallback. The agent's bef09c8 covered the no-card case and declared every path loud, missing the case where the backend initialises and then fails. Narrowing the comment and filing bwy.34 with calibration reasons is defensible given Metal's cold first call.
guidance_note: When a reviewer names a residual silent-failure class, list every way into that class before claiming it is closed.

evidence: The agent showed `lit show openconv-openconv-bwy.33` resolving and `openconv-bwy.33` erroring, so the doubled prefix is the real ID. False-positive flag: the Cargo.toml comment is original PR text, and aa074ad touched only transcribe.rs.

False-positive flag: 69a2848 only edited comments, and the guard dates from round 0. The premise is overstated: flipping the condition would make the GPU build refuse to start, which is loud, not silent, so a unit test of a one-line boolean buys little. The thread was resolved with no reply.

69a2848 (the F4 fix) added to transcribe.rs that "a compute capability the image was not built for" falls back to the CPU silently. The Dockerfile comment still says "a wrong number fails loudly at load". The thread was resolved with no reply and the packet shows no change to the Dockerfile.
guidance_note: When a fix narrows a guarantee, grep the repo for every other comment that relied on the old guarantee (here the CUDAARCHS comment) and correct it in the same commit.

narrative: Each comment or message fix produced the next finding. The F1 fix swapped one hardcoded fact for another that was false on the target that triggers it (F3). The F2 fix replaced one overclaim with a new completeness claim (F4), and narrowing that claim left the Dockerfile comment contradicting it (F7). Rounds 2 and 3 exist mainly because of those fixes. Round 3's two findings were resolved without any reply.
guidance_observations: Each fix rewrote prose about failure modes without first listing the failure modes, so every rewrite overclaimed in a new place.
Round 3 threads were resolved silently, including a correct comment-contradiction finding.

evidence: Inserting `url_for` directly below `synthesize`'s `///` block moved that doc, including "The request is made here", onto a URL formatter and left `synthesize` undocumented. The agent named the mechanism and moved the doc back.
guidance_note: When splitting a function, insert new items above the existing doc block and re-read the assembled file to check each `///` block sits on the item it describes.

evidence: Duplicate of F1: the doc block was misattached to `url_for`. Fixed by the same change in 511c734.

`answer_aloud.rs` hardcoded `model_id: None`, and `live_speech.rs` used `Voicing::default()` throughout, so neither diagnostic tool could reach the axis the PR adds. The agent threaded `OPENCONV_TTS_MODEL` through both.
guidance_note: When adding a new request axis, thread it through every example and live test that exercises that request, alongside the existing axes' env vars.

evidence: Third report of the same misattached doc block on `url_for`; fixed in 511c734.

narrative: Round 0 raised the same misattached-doc defect three times and one coverage gap in the diagnostic tools. All were fixed in 511c734, and round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent named the `///` attachment mechanism here and then repeated the same defect two days later in openconv#23 F12, so the lesson did not transfer.

evidence: `NoVoices::into_response` returned `self.0.to_string()` on an unauthenticated route, and the agent reproduced the leak of an internal URL. The fix mirrors the existing `ApiError::LiveKit` pattern of logging the cause and returning a generic body.
guidance_note: When adding an IntoResponse for an upstream failure, copy the codebase's existing upstream-error arm instead of writing a new one.

evidence: Assigning `.value` fires no `change`, so a late listing left the agent on the default. The agent reproduced this with a 3s-delayed listing and took the reviewer's re-notify option via a dispatched event. The fix only covered a call already assigned, which F4, F6 and F8 then found.
guidance_note: When fixing an ordering race, enumerate every state of the receiver at the moment the event fires (no call, call joining, call up) and verify the fix in each.

evidence: After the catch, execution fell through to the not-on-offer check, producing a second, untrue message. Moving the assignment and check inside `try` removed the conflation, verified with a control on the healthy path.
guidance_note: When code after a try/catch depends on the try having succeeded, put it inside the try.

evidence: The dispatch added in f8a3d38 hits `call?.useChosenVoice()` while `call` is still null during `Call.join()`, a silent no-op. The agent: "the dispatch I added in f8a3d38 opened it", and `null` was carrying two states.
guidance_note: When adding a second writer to a control whose handler guards on `x?.`, check what the null arm means for the new writer before relying on it.

evidence: False-positive flag: f8a3d38 touched only app.js, and the duplicated status-to-Refused block came from `voices()` in the original PR. The agent confirmed the two blocks were identical and extracted `ok_or_refused`.
guidance_note: When adding a second HTTP call to a client module, reuse or extract the first call's response handling rather than copying it.

evidence: Same mid-join null-`call` race as F4, created by the f8a3d38 dispatch, and fixed by the same `sendChosenVoice()` after assignment in 0ee1d8d.

False-positive flag: the `/call/voices` route is original PR code. The asymmetry is real, but the network accepts no inbound connections, so severity is overstated. Caching would contradict the documented reason `voices()` is uncached, and a per-route limiter is the wrong layer; the agent filed bwy.40.
This is the third report of the mid-join race opened by the f8a3d38 dispatch. The reviewer's suggestion (re-notify right after `call = await Call.join(...)`) is what landed in 0ee1d8d.

False-positive flag: f8a3d38 did not touch caller.js. The awaited `reportPresence()` came from the original PR, and the agent confirmed master did not await it. Keeping the await for ordering and detaching the rejection keeps a voice failure from aborting the join.
guidance_note: When converting a fire-and-forget call into an awaited one inside a try that tears down the session, decide explicitly whether its failure should be fatal.

evidence: The 0ee1d8d resend made the call end on the live control value while `remember(fields)` still persisted the `readForm()` snapshot taken before the join. The agent: "removed the stale copy from the call path and left one in the persistence path."
guidance_note: When a fix replaces a snapshot with a live read on one path, grep every other consumer of that snapshot and move them to the live read too.

evidence: 0ee1d8d rewrote the comment to say "Either way a rejection reaches the page's `unhandledrejection` reporter", but `queueMicrotask(() => { throw })` fires `error`. The agent verified this in the browser and correctly declined the alternative of a returned rejection, which would re-abort the join.
guidance_note: When a comment names the runtime mechanism a new helper uses, verify the mechanism (here, which global event fires) before writing it down.

evidence: The 0ee1d8d diff inserts `reportDetached` and its JSDoc between the `tellAgents` doc and `const tellAgents`, orphaning that doc. The agent had already fixed it locally in 4b43134 before the review.
guidance_note: When inserting a helper near existing code, place it above the neighbour's doc block, the same `///`-attachment lesson the agent stated in openconv#19 F1.

evidence: False-positive flag: e4c5c69 only edited comments, and the untested logic accumulated across the PR. The premise that the verification was ad hoc and uncommitted is true, but the repo runs no tests in CI at all. The agent added `web/caller.test.mjs`, mutation-checked each test, and filed bwy.41 for the live-room ordering harness.
guidance_note: When verification needs a hand-built rig, commit the part that runs without live infrastructure as a test in the same commit as the fix.

evidence: False-positive flag: a1e3fae only added a test file. The coverage gap is real, but the suggested extraction would replace the DOM readback (`els.voice.value = wanted; if (els.voice.value !== wanted)`) with a re-derived membership check, a second implementation of what the browser decides. The ordering half was already filed as bwy.41.
The F1 disclosure fix (90ec773) was made by hand with no regression test. The agent added a test over all four `TtsError` variants that fails when `self.0.to_string()` is restored.
guidance_note: When fixing a reachable-without-a-browser bug, especially a disclosure, land a regression test that fails on the old code in the same commit.

narrative: The F2 race fix (a dispatched change event) handled the call-up state but not the call-joining state. That produced three duplicate findings (F4, F6, F8), and their fix exposed a stale snapshot in the persistence path (F10). The F9 fix added a helper that misplaced a JSDoc (F12) and a comment naming the wrong global event (F11). Round 2's findings were all fix-caused, while rounds 1, 3 and 4 had independent findings, mostly test-coverage asks. The PR hit the 5-round review cap, so the final head was never reviewed.
guidance_observations: Race fixes were verified against the one ordering the reviewer described rather than against every receiver state, so each fix uncovered the next window.
Fixes landed without committed regression tests until the reviewer asked twice, which cost two test-coverage rounds.
